corrections.correction: The compute capability 8.9 minimum is a software check in vLLM 0.23, not a hardware requirement. Upstream vLLM lowered it to 8.0 (vllm-project/vllm#45306, merged as a8c86eeb) because both formats in the checkpoint already have SM80 kernels: NVFP4 experts through Marlin W4A16 and FP8 layers through Marlin W8A16. With that change backported (aml/src/nvfp4_sm80_port.json, NVFP4_SM80_PORT=1), skt/A.X-K2-NVFP4 served on one 8 x A100 node. A100 still has no FP4 or FP8 tensor cores, so these layers compute with BF16 activations.

interpretation: Up to 8K inputs the 16 A100s deliver 0.43-0.51x (native) and 0.52-0.64x (dense) of the tech report's one B200 node, i.e. roughly a quarter of its throughput per GPU: A100 has no FP8 tensor cores, so the FP8 weights run through Marlin W8A16 kernels, and decode at concurrency 32 is bound by MoE weight reads.

From 16K inputs the gap widens. The BF16 MLA KV cache is replicated on every tensor-parallel rank, so the cluster holds 673,792 tokens (native) and 766,032 (dense); only 20 of 32 requests fit at 32K, 10 at 64K and 5 at 120K, and the rest queue. The DSA indexer runs as BF16 Triton kernels replicated on each TP rank instead of DeepGEMM FP8, and its prefill cost grows with the square of the input.

Dense mode is 1.2-2.4x faster than native at the same lengths but found no needle at 126K or 253K tokens; it is only usable for contexts up to about 60K tokens (12/12 needles to 60K in the earlier run).
TP16 across the two nodes over InfiniBand is 12-41% faster than TP8 x PP2 at 1K-8K inputs (dense), with half the KV capacity (362,848 tokens), so it suits short contexts only.

EAGLE3 cannot speed up this stack on A100: TRITON_MLA's decode path accepts one query token per request (query_len_support SINGLE_ONLY), CUDA-graph start-up asserts on the 4-token verification queries (mla_attention.py:1827), and the eager fallback measured 1.05 tokens per step (draft acceptance 1.5%) and 4-5x lower throughput than TP16 without speculation.
